caption: Summer pays for winter, in theory. Anyone else's income swing this hard with the season?

slides.title:
How we spend
our R26 000
low-season income
Living in Jeffreys Bay
slides.body:
Him 30, her 28
Married, no kids yet
Jobs: Surf instructor & guesthouse housekeeper
Combined net: R26 000 p/m (low season)

slides.title: Rent
slides.includes: 2 bed cottage, two streets from Supertubes
slides.body: In December we'd fight the whole town for parking near this place. In winter it's just quiet, and the rent doesn't care.

slides.title: Bakkie instalment
slides.includes: Hauls boards and gear to lessons up and down the coast
slides.body: It's a work vehicle as much as a car, so neither of us feels bad about the payment. Most months.

slides.title: Groceries
slides.includes: Spar, the farm stall on Fridays
slides.body: Two people who surf before breakfast eat like it. This one barely moves between seasons.

slides.title: Board & gear maintenance
slides.includes: Wax, leashes, a fin he lost off the point
slides.body: Small repairs he swears he'll stop paying for the day he stops teaching. He won't.

slides.title: Takeaways & braai supplies
slides.includes: Fish and chips after a bad lesson day, braai packs for the weekend
slides.body: We told each other this was a summer habit. It is not.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: Fuel, medical aid, insurance, phone & fibre, funeral policies, stokvel
slides.body: None of these change with the season. Our income does, and that's the whole problem some months.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R26 000, and that's a low-season month. December will look nothing like this, which is exactly the problem.

slides.title: We stopped guessing
slides.body:
We uploaded three months of statements, the good ones and the quiet ones, to Beyond Horizon and it sorted every transaction for us.

Seeing July next to December in one place changed how we plan.

No bank login needed.
